verdict.summary: A real gap sits between free chatbot answers and $50-plus human research, but nothing yet shows that buyers will pay to close it.

idea.name: Single-payment business idea teardowns
idea.headline: Idea teardowns for a single $5 to $10 payment
idea.customer: First-time founders and side-project builders with an idea and no way to judge it.
idea.problem: Free advice is vague, and proper research costs more than an untested idea justifies.
idea.revenue: One payment of $5 to $10 per report. No subscription and no account.

alternatives.finding: Free chatbots below, $50-plus human research above.

demand_evidence.finding: Many ask for validation. Few visibly pay for it.

economics.finding: 85% margin, but under $6 a sale to fund growth.

distribution.finding: Price is too low to support paid acquisition.

blockers.finding: Nothing legal or technical prevents a launch.

page_summaries.market: Free answers sit below this price and expensive research sits above it. The slot in between is empty, which is either an opening or a warning.
page_summaries.business: The margin is healthy and the profit is small. Under six dollars a sale has to pay for finding the customer.
page_summaries.next_steps: Three things must be true for this to work. They are ranked by how much damage each one does if it turns out to be false.

alternatives.name: General AI chatbot
alternatives.what_it_does: Answers “is this a good idea?” in seconds from one prompt.
alternatives.weakness: Agrees with the person asking, cites nothing, and needs a skilled prompt to be useful.

alternatives.name: AI idea-validator apps
alternatives.what_it_does: A web form returns a scored validation report.

weakness.text: A subscription for a one-off need. Scores arrive without sources.

alternatives.name: Freelance research gig
alternatives.what_it_does: A freelancer writes a short market report to order.

weakness.text: Three to seven days to deliver, and quality varies by seller.

alternatives.name: Paid advisor call
alternatives.what_it_does: An hour of questions with an experienced founder.
alternatives.weakness: Costs more than the idea is worth before any test has been run.

alternatives.name: Doing it by hand
alternatives.what_it_does: Searching competitors, reviews and forums yourself.

weakness.text: Most people stop after the first search and never reach pricing.

market_gap.text: Nothing on this list is cheap, sourced and finished at once. Chatbots are free, but they agree with the person asking and show no evidence. Human research is sourced, but it starts at seven times the price and takes days.

market_gap: The open position is a fixed-format report with cited evidence, bought once for less than a lunch. The gap is real. Whether it is a market is what the tests on page 4 are for.

note.text: Idea-stage members of five founder communities
Most buy once, a few test several ideas
A ceiling. At 2% conversion it is about $31,500.

price.label: Price
price.note: Midpoint of the range, paid once

note.text: A third of the $5.95 left after costs

reason.text: Free and on target, but self-promotion rules limit how often a link can be posted.

distribution.name: Public sample teardowns
distribution.examples: Free reports published as search content

reason.text: Each sample can rank for its own idea, but search traffic takes three to six months to build.

distribution.name: Paid search and social ads
distribution.examples: Search, social and forum ad networks

reason.text: At $1 to $3 a click and 3% conversion, a customer costs 17 to 50 times the $1.98 ceiling.

detail.text: Clear terms and the disclaimer on page 4 are needed before launch.
Language models fabricate citations, so every FOUND link needs an automated check before delivery.
A threefold rise in model and search costs would cut margin from 85% to 72%.

riskiest_assumptions.statement: People will pay $5 to $10 for a sourced report when a chatbot gives a rough one for free.
riskiest_assumptions.short: People will pay for this when a general AI chatbot gives a rough version for free.
riskiest_assumptions.if_false: If false, there is no business. This is the riskiest assumption from page 1.

riskiest_assumptions.statement: Free channels alone can deliver the first 100 customers.
riskiest_assumptions.if_false: If false, the product works but nobody finds it, because the price cannot fund paid acquisition.

riskiest_assumptions.statement: A report costs about $1 to produce with every source checked and no person involved.
riskiest_assumptions.if_false: If false, margin falls and each report needs a human editor.

next_tests.name: Paid landing page.
next_tests.description: A one-page offer with a $7 checkout. Reports written by hand.
next_tests.summary: Put a one-page offer with a $7 checkout in front of 300 visitors from founder communities, and write the first reports by hand. It is the cheapest way to check the assumption above.
next_tests.kill_threshold: Fewer than 9 paid orders from 300 visitors, a rate under 3%.

next_tests.name: Five public teardowns.
next_tests.description: Free sample reports posted to three founder communities.
next_tests.kill_threshold: Fewer than 300 visits in total, or posts removed as promotion.

next_tests.name: Automated batch.
next_tests.description: Thirty reports generated with link checks and no editing.
next_tests.kill_threshold: Cost above $1.50 a report, or more than 1 dead source in 20.
